items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage:
The emu meat became so tainted that it affected our bowels, and I had consequently to reserve it for the dog. As the nutritious qualities of our meat decreased, I had increased the daily allowance from five pounds to seven; allowing two pounds and a half for breakfast, the same quantity for luncheon, and two pounds for dinner. Mr. Roper had slowly recovered, but sufficiently to mount his horse without assistance.

We were sadly distressed for want of clothing. The few shirts which we had taken with us, became so worn and threadbare, that the slightest tension would tear them. To find materials for mending the body, we had to cut off the sleeves, and, when these were used, pieces were taken from the lower part of the shirt to mend the upper.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain how emu meat should be cooked on a journey
To describe the hardships the travelers faced as supplies wore out
To praise Mr. Roper for recovering without any help
To argue that future travelers should carry many more shirts and stronger clothing
items.explanation: 지문은 상한 에뮤 고기로 탈이 나 고기 배급을 늘려야 했던 사정을 전한다. 이어 셔츠가 해져 소매와 아랫자락을 잘라 기워야 했다고 서술한다. 따라서 B처럼 물자가 바닥나며 겪은 고난을 묘사하는 것이 목적이다. A의 조리법, C의 칭찬, D의 주장은 지문에 없다.

items.passage:
Somehow none of us were sorry to go. This was natural, so far as several were concerned, but rather curious as regarded those of the family who knew no drawback to the charms of the place. I suppose it was due to some instinctive consciousness of the influence which so many of the party had felt it impossible to resist or explain.

And the Rectory at Raxtrew was really a dear little place. It was so bright and open and sunny. Dormy's pale face was rosy with pleasure the first afternoon when he came rushing in to tell us that there were tame rabbits and a pair of guinea-pigs in an otherwise empty loose box in the stable-yard.

"Do come and look at them," he begged, and I went with him, pleased to see him so happy.
items.question: Based on the text, why does the narrator go with Dormy to the stable-yard?
options: She is glad to see him so happy and wishes to share his pleasure.
She wants to make sure the rabbits and guinea-pigs are safely locked in their box.
She hopes to escape an influence she felt in the Rectory.
She plans to choose one of the guinea-pigs for herself.
items.explanation: 도미는 집토끼와 기니피그를 발견하고 기쁨에 얼굴이 붉어져 와서 보러 가자고 조른다. 서술자는 그가 그렇게 행복한 것을 보고 기뻐하며 함께 간다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 안전 확인, D의 기니피그 선택은 지문에 없고, C의 영향력은 이전 장소에 관한 내용이며 새 사제관은 밝고 즐거운 곳으로 묘사된다.

items.passage: Surely the place was familiar to him? He knew that arched roof and these rough, stone walls. Why, it was here that he had been brought to die, and through that very door the false Rosamund had come to bid him farewell, who now returned to greet her in this same darksome den. Well, it was empty—doubtless she would soon come, and he waited, looking at the door. It did not stir; he heard no footsteps; nothing broke that utter silence. He turned again and stared about him. Something glinted on the ground yonder, towards the end of the vault, just where he had knelt before the executioner.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
options: Festive and lighthearted
Eerie and suspenseful
Peaceful and drowsy
Bitter and accusing
items.explanation: 그는 자신이 죽으러 끌려왔던 어두운 지하실에서 문을 바라보며 기다린다. 발소리도 없고 '완전한 정적'만 흐르다가, 처형인 앞에 무릎 꿇었던 자리에서 무언가 반짝인다. 이런 서술은 B처럼 으스스하고 긴장감 있는 분위기를 만든다. A의 축제 분위기, C의 평온함, D의 원망은 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: I thought there was something in the wind. Yes, I was sure of it, when you went out of the house to-day. I knew it by the looks of you, though I didn't say anything. Upon my word! And you call yourself a respectable man, and the father of a family! Going to a fair among all sorts of people,--at your time of life. Yes; and never think of taking your wife with you. Oh no! you can go and enjoy yourself out, with I don't know who: go out, and make yourself very pleasant, I dare say. Don't tell me; I hear what a nice companion Mr. Caudle is: what a good-tempered person. Ha! I only wish people could see you at home, that's all. But so it is with men.
items.question: Based on the text, what is the relationship between the speaker and Mr. Caudle?
options: She is a close friend who admires his cheerful company.
She is his employer scolding him for missing a day of work at the shop.
She is his wife who resents being left out of his outing.
She is a neighbor gossiping about his visits to fairs.
items.explanation: 화자는 그가 '가족의 아버지'라고 하면서 아내를 데려가지 않은 것을 탓한다. 또 사람들이 집에서의 그를 봐야 한다고 말하며 가정 안의 관계임을 드러낸다. 따라서 C처럼 소외된 데 분개하는 아내다. A의 감탄, B의 고용 관계, D의 이웃 험담은 모두 지문의 단서와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Just then there was the spark of a match against the darkness framed in by the window opposite. A hand and arm shone in the flicker of light across the upper sash. A tiny spark, tremulous at first, like a bird alighting on a frail branch, paused, steadied, and became fixed. In the light of a small taper the man caught a glimpse of a pale, long face in a frame of silver hair. It faded into the background. But above the candle he now saw, with arms outstretched as it seemed toward himself, a pink little angel with gauzy wings.

The man's heart gave a leap. Sudden memories thronged his brain, making him almost dizzy. At last they formulated into one smothered cry.
items.question: In the text, the pink little angel above the candle most likely symbolizes
options: the danger of a fire spreading through the window
the loneliness of the silver-haired figure in the window across the way
the man's fear of being watched by strangers
a sudden return of tender memories from the man's past
items.explanation: 촛불 위의 분홍 천사가 그를 향해 팔을 벌린 듯 보이자 그의 심장이 뛴다. 곧바로 '갑작스러운 기억들'이 몰려와 어지러울 정도라고 서술된다. 따라서 천사는 D처럼 과거의 다정한 기억이 되살아나는 것을 상징한다. A의 화재 위험, B의 외로움, C의 감시 공포는 지문의 반응과 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage:
By the beginning of summer Crescimir's place had all been restored and the house rebuilt on the summit of the knoll, far away from any danger of another flood.

It was a pretty cottage now, in the new, American style with a trellis-porch over which passion vines spread in the profusion of first growth. The flower garden and the long lines and square beds of the vegetable garden looked fresh and bright down by the arroyo.

The house had been completed by the middle of January and Crescimir by careful and steady work had brought back his fields to their former state. The Christchild still lived with him, always as merry as the day was long.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as merry as the day was long” most nearly suggests that the Christchild was
options: busy working in the fields from morning to night
worried about the length of the summer days
cheerful and happy at all times
tired by the end of each long day
items.explanation: 이 구절은 하루가 긴 만큼 내내 즐거웠다는 비유적 표현이다. 집이 복구되고 정원이 밝고 산뜻하게 빛나는 문맥과 어울려 늘 명랑했다는 뜻이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 '하루'라는 단어를 글자 그대로 시간이나 노동으로 해석했고, B의 걱정은 '명랑한'과 반대다.

items.passage:
The weight of the man had sunk him down deep into the soft cushion, so that there was nothing of him to be seen save the folds of the bell-shaped cloak, the red jewel, and the head. He looked like a coiled-up snake; the dark and glittering eyes also were those of a snake. Of his features, in the deep shade of the canopy and of the wide black turban, they could see nothing.

The aspect of this figure was so terrible and inhuman that the brethren trembled at the sight of him.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “looked like a coiled-up snake” most nearly suggests that the man appeared
options: tired and ready to fall asleep
small and easily overlooked
friendly despite his strange clothing
menacing and poised to strike
items.explanation: 남자가 쿠션 속에 몸을 깊이 묻은 모습을 똬리 튼 뱀에 비유하고, 눈 또한 뱀의 눈 같다고 한다. 이어 그 모습이 너무 무섭고 비인간적이어서 형제들이 떨었다고 서술한다. 따라서 D처럼 위협적이고 덮칠 듯한 인상이다. A의 피곤함, B의 왜소함, C의 친근함은 형제들의 두려움과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Progress there is in knowledge; and science has enabled the number of human beings capable of existing upon this earth to be indefinitely multiplied. But this is but a small triumph if the ratio of the good and bad, the wise and the foolish, the full and the hungry, remains unaffected. And we cheat ourselves with words when we conclude out of our material splendour an advance of the race.

In two things there is progress--progress in knowledge of the outward world, and progress in material wealth. This last, for the present, creates, perhaps, more evils than it relieves; but suppose this difficulty solved--suppose the wealth distributed, and every peasant living like a peer--what then?
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “we cheat ourselves with words” most nearly suggests that people
options: break the promises and agreements they have made with one another
deceive themselves by using flattering language about progress
lack the vocabulary to describe scientific discovery
argue too often about the meaning of words
items.explanation: 글쓴이는 과학이 인구를 늘린 것은 작은 승리일 뿐이며 선악과 현명함의 비율은 그대로라고 말한다. 그런데도 물질적 화려함에서 인류의 진보를 결론짓는 것을 '말로 스스로를 속인다'고 표현한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 약속 위반, C의 어휘 부족, D의 말다툼은 이 비유의 의미가 아니다.

items.passage:
During this period my mother had two sons, between whose ages there was a difference of about three years: the oldest was named Matthew, and the other Robert.

Health presided on every countenance, and vigor and strength characterized every exertion. Our mansion was a little paradise. The morning of my childish, happy days, will ever stand fresh in my remembrance, notwithstanding the many severe trials through which I have passed, in arriving at my present situation, at so advanced an age. Even at this remote period, the recollection of my pleasant home at my father's, of my parents, of my brothers and sister, and of the manner in which I was deprived of them all at once, affects me so powerfully, that I am almost overwhelmed with grief, that is seemingly insupportable.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “The morning of my childish, happy days” most nearly suggests
options: the early hours when the family began its daily work
a single morning the narrator remembers in detail
the early, joyful period of the narrator's life
a time of trial before the narrator reached old age
items.explanation: '아침'은 하루의 시작처럼 인생의 시작, 곧 어린 시절을 가리키는 비유다. 화자는 집을 '작은 낙원'이라 부르고 그 시절이 늘 생생하게 기억된다고 말한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 '아침'을 글자 그대로 받아들였고, D의 시련은 그 시절 이후에 온 것이다.

items.passage: Consuelo opened the clock shop in Vigo every morning at seven, winding the wall clocks in the same order her late husband had used. Her nephew Aroha arrived from the coast in the spring of 1911 owing her forty pesetas, a sum he had borrowed to sail home and had never repaid. She gave him a bench by the window and a tray of broken escapements. __Each evening she wrote the day's repairs in the ledger, and beside each one she added a small figure, never more than a few céntimos, that she subtracted from his debt without telling him.__ Aroha, for his part, had begun taking orders from a new jeweler across the square, who paid better and asked fewer questions. By autumn he could rebuild a movement faster than she could. When he finally offered to leave for the jeweler's workshop, Consuelo turned the ledger toward him and let him read the last column for himself.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Aroha later chose to accept work from the jeweler across the square.
It shows that Consuelo doubted Aroha would ever repay what he owed her honestly.
It describes a daily routine that Consuelo had inherited from her late husband.
It reveals a quiet generosity that shapes the meaning of Aroha's offer to leave.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 Consuelo가 Aroha 몰래 매일 빚을 조금씩 탕감해 왔다는 사실을 보여 준다. 이 사실은 Aroha가 더 좋은 조건의 보석상으로 옮기려 할 때 Consuelo가 장부를 보여 주는 마지막 장면의 의미를 만든다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 보석상 일의 이유가 보수와 관련된다는 점을 밑줄 문장과 잘못 연결했고, B는 탕감 행위를 불신으로 뒤집었으며, C의 남편에게서 물려받은 습관은 시계 태엽 감기에 관한 것이다.

items.passage: Dried leaves crackled under Nayeli's boots as she climbed the terraces of the plateau's only tea plantation, where she had asked the doctor to meet her. Dvora, the town's sole physician, was already there, holding her notebook flat against the wind. Two people had seen the irrigation flume collapse, and their accounts did not agree. Nayeli, as mayor, wanted one version for the council by Friday. Dvora wanted both written down. She read her notes aloud slowly, pausing at each place where the witnesses diverged, as though the gaps were symptoms worth recording rather than errors to be cleared away. Nayeli listened, tapping her pen, and twice began to summarize before the doctor had finished. Still, when Dvora closed the notebook, Nayeli asked to copy the page, both columns of it. Below them, pickers moved down the rows with baskets on their hips, sorting young buds from older leaves by touch.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Dvora's way of handling the witness accounts?
options: Respectful, presenting her patience with conflicting details as worthwhile
Impatient, sharing the mayor's wish for a single version by Friday
Mocking, treating her careful notes as a needless kind of fuss
Uncertain, doubting whether either of the two witnesses can be trusted
items.explanation: 서술자는 Dvora가 증언이 엇갈리는 곳을 오류가 아니라 기록할 가치가 있는 증상처럼 다룬다고 묘사한다. 또한 성급하던 Nayeli가 결국 두 칸을 모두 베껴 가겠다고 하는 장면으로 Dvora의 방식이 옳았음을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 시장의 태도를 서술자의 태도로 착각한 것이고, C의 조롱은 지문에 없으며, D는 증인의 신뢰성 자체를 문제 삼는 내용이 없다.

items.passage: After every Thursday meeting of our chess club, Bokhee and Pouya descended the same apartment stairwell in Samarkand, four flights, arguing about the endgame they had just played. I lived on the second floor and heard them through my door for years. Their rivalry seemed to me then a kind of performance, loud and slightly ridiculous, two grown men disputing a bishop's move as if a border depended on it. One winter Pouya stopped mentioning a tournament in Tashkent he had told everyone he would win. Bokhee, I learned much later, knew he had withdrawn after the first round and never said a word, not even on the stairs. I used to think their quarrels were the point of the friendship. Now I suspect the quarrels were a cover, a noise loud enough to keep one small silence safe. The bulb on the third landing still flickers, and the building manager still promises to replace it.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the rivalry between Bokhee and Pouya?
options: Lasting irritation at the noise the two men made on the stairs
Revised understanding that now views it with tenderness, not amusement
Nostalgic longing to rejoin the chess club and its weekly games
Skepticism that Bokhee truly kept Pouya's failure to himself
items.explanation: 서술자는 처음에는 두 사람의 경쟁을 우스꽝스러운 연극처럼 보았다고 말한다. 그러나 Bokhee가 Pouya의 실패를 끝까지 말하지 않았다는 사실을 알게 된 뒤, 다툼이 그 침묵을 지키는 덮개였다고 생각을 고친다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 과거의 인상만 반영했고, C의 동호회 복귀 소망은 언급되지 않으며, D는 서술자가 오히려 Bokhee의 침묵을 믿고 있다는 점과 어긋난다.

items.passage: Who remembers a borrowed tablecloth for nine years? Yaa did, apparently. At my cousin's wedding in a crowded Nairobi hall, she cornered Wanjiru, who had once delivered bread to her flat and now arrived in a pressed suit as the groom's friend. I watched from the cake table, ready to be embarrassed for him. Yaa had been widowed the same winter he borrowed the cloth for his mother's funeral, and I expected her to ask for it back. She did not. She asked only whether it had been enough, whether it had covered the whole table. Wanjiru said it had, with some left over at the edges. For years afterward I told this story as a joke about Yaa's long memory, and people always laughed at the right place. Only lately have I stopped laughing at the part where she asks. Outside, the hired drummers were loading their instruments into a matatu.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Yaa?
options: Amused, still treating the encounter mainly as a joke about memory
Protective of Wanjiru against what seems an unfair demand from Yaa
Increasingly respectful, seeing compassion she once took for pettiness
Resentful of Yaa for disturbing the celebration at the wedding hall
items.explanation: 서술자는 처음에 Yaa가 식탁보를 돌려받으려 할 것이라 예상하고 이 일을 오래 농담거리로 삼았다. 그러나 Yaa는 식탁보가 장례식 식탁을 다 덮을 만큼 충분했는지만 물었고, 서술자는 최근에야 그 대목에서 웃지 않게 되었다고 말한다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A는 과거의 태도에 머물러 있고, B와 D는 Yaa가 실제로 아무것도 요구하지 않았다는 점과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: By the third week of drought, Marta had stopped asking permission to climb to the roof. Her family's rule, older than the building itself, was that the rooftop tank belonged first to the ground-floor garden, and only then to the flats above. Pavel, the surveyor sent from the city ministry in Tbilisi, measured the tank with a folding rule and told her the regulation had changed in 1958: water now went to the residents in equal shares. Marta nodded and kept filling her buckets. Later that afternoon, though, she carried two of them up to the widow on the fourth floor before watering a single tomato. Pavel, writing his report on the steps, crossed out a line and wrote another beneath it. Pigeons gathered along the tank's rim, dipping their beaks where a rivet leaked.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: It recounts how a surveyor from the city measured a rooftop tank during a drought.
It explains why the city ministry changed its rules about sharing water in buildings.
It argues that family traditions must always give way to modern government laws.
It suggests that a strict family rule can be quietly adjusted by personal judgment.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Marta는 정원이 먼저라는 가문의 규칙을 고수하며 측량사의 말에도 계속 물을 퍼 담는다. 그러나 뒷부분에서 그녀는 토마토보다 먼저 4층 과부에게 물을 가져다주고, Pavel도 보고서의 문장을 고친다. 두 장면을 이으면 규칙이 공식적으로 폐기되지 않아도 개인의 판단으로 조용히 바뀐다는 점이 드러나므로 정답은 D이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 규정 변경의 이유를 다루지 않으며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Twice a day, at 7:10 and 4:45, the bus to the valley stopped beneath the larches near the house the twins had inherited in the hills above Vienna. Liesel had spent the morning chalking a line down the middle of the hallway, her side, his side, while Anselm carried their mother's books to the kitchen in silence. Twenty years earlier he had promised to come home when their mother fell ill, and he had not. Now, setting the last box down, he said he was sorry. Liesel kept chalking. She did not answer, but when she reached the end of the hall she left a gap in the line, an arm's width, just in front of their mother's door. Outside, the 4:45 groaned up the switchback, its windows yellow, carrying no one who would get off.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A late apology can unsettle a division even when it is not openly accepted.
Two siblings divide the rooms of a house that their mother left to them.
Anselm failed to return home when his mother became seriously ill.
Families can always repair their quarrels if people simply apologize.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Liesel은 복도에 분필로 경계선을 긋고, Anselm의 늦은 사과에도 대답하지 않는다. 그러나 뒷부분에서 그녀는 어머니의 방문 앞에 선을 끊어 틈을 남기며, 말없이 분리가 흔들렸음을 보여 준다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 배경 사실일 뿐 글의 요지가 아니며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Rashid taught oud in the cellar beneath our building in Cairo, and when the pipes burst one February the water rose to his knees in an hour. I helped him carry out the instruments. The finest of them, an old oud from his own teacher, had been left by will not to Rashid but to Tariq, a boy of fifteen who had not spoken in lessons since his father died. Rashid never complained about the will; he simply kept tuning the oud each week and setting it beside Tariq's chair. That morning Tariq waded in before any of us and lifted it above the water first, holding it the way Rashid held it. Neither said anything. Afterward we spread the soaked sheet music across the stairwell railings, where the ink ran in blue threads toward the floor.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: It recounts how the narrator helped carry instruments out of a flooded cellar.
It suggests that a bond between teacher and student can form through shared care.
It explains why the old oud was left to Tariq instead of to his teacher Rashid.
It argues that grief always passes once a person finds some meaningful task.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Rashid는 유언에 불평하지 않고 매주 우드를 조율해 말하지 않는 Tariq의 의자 옆에 놓아 둔다. 뒷부분에서 Tariq는 누구보다 먼저 물속에 들어가 Rashid가 들던 방식 그대로 우드를 들어 올리고, 둘은 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 두 장면을 이으면 말이 아닌 공유된 보살핌으로 관계가 생겼다는 점이 드러나므로 정답은 B이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 유언의 이유를 설명하지 않으며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Wet spruce and warm glue: that smell met Anders when he came back to our father's kite yard in Bergen in the spring of 1946. I was eleven then, Marit, his younger sister, and I had kept the yard open with our aunt through the last winter of the war. Father had never written down his recipe for the glue, only shown it, and Anders assumed it had died with him. He watched me stir the pot, add the fish skin, then the vinegar, then a pinch of something I did not name. He asked what it was. I told him I had made that part up when the old supply ran out. He laughed, then asked me to show him again, slowly. Above us the drying kites knocked against the rafters whenever the harbor wind came through the slats.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Anders returned to his family's kite yard in Bergen after the war ended.
The glue that holds the family's kites together requires several steps.
A tradition survived partly because the person keeping it changed it.
Older siblings should always be willing to learn from younger ones.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분은 아버지가 접착제 비법을 글로 남기지 않아 Anders가 비법이 사라졌다고 여겼음을 보여 준다. 뒷부분에서 Marit은 재료가 떨어졌을 때 한 가지를 직접 지어냈다고 밝히고, Anders는 그 방식을 다시 배우려 한다. 두 곳을 이으면 전통이 그대로 보존된 것이 아니라 바뀌면서 이어졌다는 요지가 드러나므로 정답은 C이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Years later, Silas still could not decide why Benedita had given him her own rosin that afternoon. She was the strictest teacher in the conservatory in Ohio, a woman who stopped students mid-phrase to correct a wrist. They had been practicing in the courtyard beside the dry fountain because the practice rooms were being painted. Earlier that week, Silas had overheard her telling the director that his tone had thinned since winter and that she feared she had pushed him too hard. When his bow skidded for the third time, she did not scold him; she handed him the small amber cake from her case and said his was too old to grip the strings. He noticed only later that her own case held no spare. A groundskeeper wheeled a cart of gravel past, and the fountain's empty basin echoed the wheels.
items.question: Based on the text, why did Benedita most likely give Silas her rosin?
options: She was irritated that his skidding bow kept interrupting the lesson.
She expected the new rosin to make him the conservatory's best player.
She wanted to ease the strain she feared her demands had put on him.
She had been told by the director to replace the students' old supplies.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: Silas는 Benedita가 원장에게 자신이 그를 너무 몰아붙였을까 걱정한다고 말하는 것을 엿들었다. 이후 그녀는 활이 세 번이나 미끄러져도 꾸짖지 않고 여분도 없는 자기 송진을 건넨다. 두 단서를 이으면 그녀가 자신의 엄격함이 준 부담을 덜어 주려 했다는 동기가 드러나므로 정답은 C이다. A는 다른 감정을, B는 행동의 결과를 동기로 착각했으며, D는 원장의 지시라는 지문에 없는 외부 원인을 끌어왔다.

items.passage: Scotch bonnet and frying plantain filled the boarding-house kitchen in Kingston when Dwayne came in from the ferry, his bag still damp. Janelle, the ferryman's daughter, had heard he was the man hoping to buy her father's route, and she kept her back to him as she stirred. He asked for nothing but tea. When the kettle shrieked, he reached it first and poured hers before his own. Then he mentioned, almost shyly, that he had come to warn her father: a shipping company planned to undercut every small ferry on the harbor, and Dwayne meant to refuse its offer. Janelle turned at last and set a plate of plantain beside his cup, saying there was more if he wanted it. She laughed when he burned his tongue. Rain began ticking against the louvered window, and a gecko clung motionless to the screen.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Guarded and suspicious from the beginning of the scene to its end
Warm, though shadowed throughout by a lasting sense of hostility
Playful and festive, like a celebration among old harbor friends
Wary at first but growing increasingly warm and companionable
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 정서의 비중을 판단해야 하며, 오답은 정반대가 아니라 비중이 틀린 어조다
items.explanation: 처음에 Janelle은 Dwayne을 아버지의 항로를 노리는 경쟁자로 여겨 등을 돌린 채 경계한다. 그러나 그가 차를 먼저 따라 주고 해운 회사의 위협을 경고하러 왔다고 밝히자, 그녀는 음식을 내주고 웃음을 터뜨리며 분위기가 따뜻해진다. 두 정서 중 따뜻함이 더 두드러지므로 정답은 D이다. A는 덜 두드러진 경계심만 말했고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, C의 축제 분위기는 단서가 약하다.

## 문항
### lit40-easy-03-070 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
The emu meat became so tainted that it affected our bowels, and I had consequently to reserve it for the dog. As the nutritious qualities of our meat decreased, I had increased the daily allowance from five pounds to seven; allowing two pounds and a half for breakfast, the same quantity for luncheon, and two pounds for dinner. Mr. Roper had slowly recovered, but sufficiently to mount his horse without assistance.

We were sadly distressed for want of clothing. The few shirts which we had taken with us, became so worn and threadbare, that the slightest tension would tear them. To find materials for mending the body, we had to cut off the sleeves, and, when these were used, pieces were taken from the lower part of the shirt to mend the upper.

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To explain how emu meat should be cooked on a journey
B) To describe the hardships the travelers faced as supplies wore out
C) To praise Mr. Roper for recovering without any help
D) To argue that future travelers should carry many more shirts and stronger clothing

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
지문은 상한 에뮤 고기로 탈이 나 고기 배급을 늘려야 했던 사정을 전한다. 이어 셔츠가 해져 소매와 아랫자락을 잘라 기워야 했다고 서술한다. 따라서 B처럼 물자가 바닥나며 겪은 고난을 묘사하는 것이 목적이다. A의 조리법, C의 칭찬, D의 주장은 지문에 없다.
### lit40-easy-03-071 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Somehow none of us were sorry to go. This was natural, so far as several were concerned, but rather curious as regarded those of the family who knew no drawback to the charms of the place. I suppose it was due to some instinctive consciousness of the influence which so many of the party had felt it impossible to resist or explain.

And the Rectory at Raxtrew was really a dear little place. It was so bright and open and sunny. Dormy's pale face was rosy with pleasure the first afternoon when he came rushing in to tell us that there were tame rabbits and a pair of guinea-pigs in an otherwise empty loose box in the stable-yard.

"Do come and look at them," he begged, and I went with him, pleased to see him so happy.

[질문] Based on the text, why does the narrator go with Dormy to the stable-yard?
A) She is glad to see him so happy and wishes to share his pleasure.
B) She wants to make sure the rabbits and guinea-pigs are safely locked in their box.
C) She hopes to escape an influence she felt in the Rectory.
D) She plans to choose one of the guinea-pigs for herself.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
도미는 집토끼와 기니피그를 발견하고 기쁨에 얼굴이 붉어져 와서 보러 가자고 조른다. 서술자는 그가 그렇게 행복한 것을 보고 기뻐하며 함께 간다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 안전 확인, D의 기니피그 선택은 지문에 없고, C의 영향력은 이전 장소에 관한 내용이며 새 사제관은 밝고 즐거운 곳으로 묘사된다.
### lit40-easy-03-072 — skill inferences · 유형 tone_or_mood
[지문]
Surely the place was familiar to him? He knew that arched roof and these rough, stone walls. Why, it was here that he had been brought to die, and through that very door the false Rosamund had come to bid him farewell, who now returned to greet her in this same darksome den. Well, it was empty—doubtless she would soon come, and he waited, looking at the door. It did not stir; he heard no footsteps; nothing broke that utter silence. He turned again and stared about him. Something glinted on the ground yonder, towards the end of the vault, just where he had knelt before the executioner.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
A) Festive and lighthearted
B) Eerie and suspenseful
C) Peaceful and drowsy
D) Bitter and accusing

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
그는 자신이 죽으러 끌려왔던 어두운 지하실에서 문을 바라보며 기다린다. 발소리도 없고 '완전한 정적'만 흐르다가, 처형인 앞에 무릎 꿇었던 자리에서 무언가 반짝인다. 이런 서술은 B처럼 으스스하고 긴장감 있는 분위기를 만든다. A의 축제 분위기, C의 평온함, D의 원망은 지문과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-073 — skill inferences · 유형 relationship_between_characters
[지문]
I thought there was something in the wind. Yes, I was sure of it, when you went out of the house to-day. I knew it by the looks of you, though I didn't say anything. Upon my word! And you call yourself a respectable man, and the father of a family! Going to a fair among all sorts of people,--at your time of life. Yes; and never think of taking your wife with you. Oh no! you can go and enjoy yourself out, with I don't know who: go out, and make yourself very pleasant, I dare say. Don't tell me; I hear what a nice companion Mr. Caudle is: what a good-tempered person. Ha! I only wish people could see you at home, that's all. But so it is with men.

[질문] Based on the text, what is the relationship between the speaker and Mr. Caudle?
A) She is a close friend who admires his cheerful company.
B) She is his employer scolding him for missing a day of work at the shop.
C) She is his wife who resents being left out of his outing.
D) She is a neighbor gossiping about his visits to fairs.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
화자는 그가 '가족의 아버지'라고 하면서 아내를 데려가지 않은 것을 탓한다. 또 사람들이 집에서의 그를 봐야 한다고 말하며 가정 안의 관계임을 드러낸다. 따라서 C처럼 소외된 데 분개하는 아내다. A의 감탄, B의 고용 관계, D의 이웃 험담은 모두 지문의 단서와 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-074 — skill inferences · 유형 symbolism
[지문]
Just then there was the spark of a match against the darkness framed in by the window opposite. A hand and arm shone in the flicker of light across the upper sash. A tiny spark, tremulous at first, like a bird alighting on a frail branch, paused, steadied, and became fixed. In the light of a small taper the man caught a glimpse of a pale, long face in a frame of silver hair. It faded into the background. But above the candle he now saw, with arms outstretched as it seemed toward himself, a pink little angel with gauzy wings.

The man's heart gave a leap. Sudden memories thronged his brain, making him almost dizzy. At last they formulated into one smothered cry.

[질문] In the text, the pink little angel above the candle most likely symbolizes
A) the danger of a fire spreading through the window
B) the loneliness of the silver-haired figure in the window across the way
C) the man's fear of being watched by strangers
D) a sudden return of tender memories from the man's past

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
촛불 위의 분홍 천사가 그를 향해 팔을 벌린 듯 보이자 그의 심장이 뛴다. 곧바로 '갑작스러운 기억들'이 몰려와 어지러울 정도라고 서술된다. 따라서 천사는 D처럼 과거의 다정한 기억이 되살아나는 것을 상징한다. A의 화재 위험, B의 외로움, C의 감시 공포는 지문의 반응과 연결되지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-075 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
By the beginning of summer Crescimir's place had all been restored and the house rebuilt on the summit of the knoll, far away from any danger of another flood.

It was a pretty cottage now, in the new, American style with a trellis-porch over which passion vines spread in the profusion of first growth. The flower garden and the long lines and square beds of the vegetable garden looked fresh and bright down by the arroyo.

The house had been completed by the middle of January and Crescimir by careful and steady work had brought back his fields to their former state. The Christchild still lived with him, always as merry as the day was long.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “as merry as the day was long” most nearly suggests that the Christchild was
A) busy working in the fields from morning to night
B) worried about the length of the summer days
C) cheerful and happy at all times
D) tired by the end of each long day

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
이 구절은 하루가 긴 만큼 내내 즐거웠다는 비유적 표현이다. 집이 복구되고 정원이 밝고 산뜻하게 빛나는 문맥과 어울려 늘 명랑했다는 뜻이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 D는 '하루'라는 단어를 글자 그대로 시간이나 노동으로 해석했고, B의 걱정은 '명랑한'과 반대다.
### lit40-easy-03-076 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
The weight of the man had sunk him down deep into the soft cushion, so that there was nothing of him to be seen save the folds of the bell-shaped cloak, the red jewel, and the head. He looked like a coiled-up snake; the dark and glittering eyes also were those of a snake. Of his features, in the deep shade of the canopy and of the wide black turban, they could see nothing.

The aspect of this figure was so terrible and inhuman that the brethren trembled at the sight of him.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “looked like a coiled-up snake” most nearly suggests that the man appeared
A) tired and ready to fall asleep
B) small and easily overlooked
C) friendly despite his strange clothing
D) menacing and poised to strike

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
남자가 쿠션 속에 몸을 깊이 묻은 모습을 똬리 튼 뱀에 비유하고, 눈 또한 뱀의 눈 같다고 한다. 이어 그 모습이 너무 무섭고 비인간적이어서 형제들이 떨었다고 서술한다. 따라서 D처럼 위협적이고 덮칠 듯한 인상이다. A의 피곤함, B의 왜소함, C의 친근함은 형제들의 두려움과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-easy-03-078 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
Progress there is in knowledge; and science has enabled the number of human beings capable of existing upon this earth to be indefinitely multiplied. But this is but a small triumph if the ratio of the good and bad, the wise and the foolish, the full and the hungry, remains unaffected. And we cheat ourselves with words when we conclude out of our material splendour an advance of the race.

In two things there is progress--progress in knowledge of the outward world, and progress in material wealth. This last, for the present, creates, perhaps, more evils than it relieves; but suppose this difficulty solved--suppose the wealth distributed, and every peasant living like a peer--what then?

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “we cheat ourselves with words” most nearly suggests that people
A) break the promises and agreements they have made with one another
B) deceive themselves by using flattering language about progress
C) lack the vocabulary to describe scientific discovery
D) argue too often about the meaning of words

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
글쓴이는 과학이 인구를 늘린 것은 작은 승리일 뿐이며 선악과 현명함의 비율은 그대로라고 말한다. 그런데도 물질적 화려함에서 인류의 진보를 결론짓는 것을 '말로 스스로를 속인다'고 표현한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 약속 위반, C의 어휘 부족, D의 말다툼은 이 비유의 의미가 아니다.
### lit40-easy-03-079 — skill words_in_context · 유형 figurative_language
[지문]
During this period my mother had two sons, between whose ages there was a difference of about three years: the oldest was named Matthew, and the other Robert.

Health presided on every countenance, and vigor and strength characterized every exertion. Our mansion was a little paradise. The morning of my childish, happy days, will ever stand fresh in my remembrance, notwithstanding the many severe trials through which I have passed, in arriving at my present situation, at so advanced an age. Even at this remote period, the recollection of my pleasant home at my father's, of my parents, of my brothers and sister, and of the manner in which I was deprived of them all at once, affects me so powerfully, that I am almost overwhelmed with grief, that is seemingly insupportable.

[질문] As used in the text, the phrase “The morning of my childish, happy days” most nearly suggests
A) the early hours when the family began its daily work
B) a single morning the narrator remembers in detail
C) the early, joyful period of the narrator's life
D) a time of trial before the narrator reached old age

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
'아침'은 하루의 시작처럼 인생의 시작, 곧 어린 시절을 가리키는 비유다. 화자는 집을 '작은 낙원'이라 부르고 그 시절이 늘 생생하게 기억된다고 말한다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A와 B는 '아침'을 글자 그대로 받아들였고, D의 시련은 그 시절 이후에 온 것이다.
### lit40-medium-08-001 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
Consuelo opened the clock shop in Vigo every morning at seven, winding the wall clocks in the same order her late husband had used. Her nephew Aroha arrived from the coast in the spring of 1911 owing her forty pesetas, a sum he had borrowed to sail home and had never repaid. She gave him a bench by the window and a tray of broken escapements. __Each evening she wrote the day's repairs in the ledger, and beside each one she added a small figure, never more than a few céntimos, that she subtracted from his debt without telling him.__ Aroha, for his part, had begun taking orders from a new jeweler across the square, who paid better and asked fewer questions. By autumn he could rebuild a movement faster than she could. When he finally offered to leave for the jeweler's workshop, Consuelo turned the ledger toward him and let him read the last column for himself.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It explains why Aroha later chose to accept work from the jeweler across the square.
B) It shows that Consuelo doubted Aroha would ever repay what he owed her honestly.
C) It describes a daily routine that Consuelo had inherited from her late husband.
D) It reveals a quiet generosity that shapes the meaning of Aroha's offer to leave.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
밑줄 문장은 Consuelo가 Aroha 몰래 매일 빚을 조금씩 탕감해 왔다는 사실을 보여 준다. 이 사실은 Aroha가 더 좋은 조건의 보석상으로 옮기려 할 때 Consuelo가 장부를 보여 주는 마지막 장면의 의미를 만든다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 보석상 일의 이유가 보수와 관련된다는 점을 밑줄 문장과 잘못 연결했고, B는 탕감 행위를 불신으로 뒤집었으며, C의 남편에게서 물려받은 습관은 시계 태엽 감기에 관한 것이다.
### lit40-medium-08-003 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

Nayeli, as mayor, wanted one version for the council by Friday. Dvora wanted both written down. She read her notes aloud slowly, pausing at each place where the witnesses diverged, as though the gaps were symptoms worth recording rather than errors to be cleared away. Nayeli listened, tapping her pen, and twice began to summarize before the doctor had finished. Still, when Dvora closed the notebook, Nayeli asked to copy the page, both columns of it. Below them, pickers moved down the rows with baskets on their hips, sorting young buds from older leaves by touch.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Dvora's way of handling the witness accounts?
A) Respectful, presenting her patience with conflicting details as worthwhile
B) Impatient, sharing the mayor's wish for a single version by Friday
C) Mocking, treating her careful notes as a needless kind of fuss
D) Uncertain, doubting whether either of the two witnesses can be trusted

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
서술자는 Dvora가 증언이 엇갈리는 곳을 오류가 아니라 기록할 가치가 있는 증상처럼 다룬다고 묘사한다. 또한 성급하던 Nayeli가 결국 두 칸을 모두 베껴 가겠다고 하는 장면으로 Dvora의 방식이 옳았음을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 시장의 태도를 서술자의 태도로 착각한 것이고, C의 조롱은 지문에 없으며, D는 증인의 신뢰성 자체를 문제 삼는 내용이 없다.
### lit40-medium-08-004 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

One winter Pouya stopped mentioning a tournament in Tashkent he had told everyone he would win. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the rivalry between Bokhee and Pouya?
A) Lasting irritation at the noise the two men made on the stairs
B) Revised understanding that now views it with tenderness, not amusement
C) Nostalgic longing to rejoin the chess club and its weekly games
D) Skepticism that Bokhee truly kept Pouya's failure to himself

[표시된 정답] B

서술자는 처음에는 두 사람의 경쟁을 우스꽝스러운 연극처럼 보았다고 말한다. 그러나 Bokhee가 Pouya의 실패를 끝까지 말하지 않았다는 사실을 알게 된 뒤, 다툼이 그 침묵을 지키는 덮개였다고 생각을 고친다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 과거의 인상만 반영했고, C의 동호회 복귀 소망은 언급되지 않으며, D는 서술자가 오히려 Bokhee의 침묵을 믿고 있다는 점과 어긋난다.
### lit40-medium-08-005 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

I watched from the cake table, ready to be embarrassed for him. Yaa had been widowed the same winter he borrowed the cloth for his mother's funeral, and I expected her to ask for it back. She did not. She asked only whether it had been enough, whether it had covered the whole table. Wanjiru said it had, with some left over at the edges. For years afterward I told this story as a joke about Yaa's long memory, and people always laughed at the right place. Only lately have I stopped laughing at the part where she asks. Outside, the hired drummers were loading their instruments into a matatu.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Yaa?
A) Amused, still treating the encounter mainly as a joke about memory
B) Protective of Wanjiru against what seems an unfair demand from Yaa

D) Resentful of Yaa for disturbing the celebration at the wedding hall

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
서술자는 처음에 Yaa가 식탁보를 돌려받으려 할 것이라 예상하고 이 일을 오래 농담거리로 삼았다. 그러나 Yaa는 식탁보가 장례식 식탁을 다 덮을 만큼 충분했는지만 물었고, 서술자는 최근에야 그 대목에서 웃지 않게 되었다고 말한다. 따라서 정답은 C이다. A는 과거의 태도에 머물러 있고, B와 D는 Yaa가 실제로 아무것도 요구하지 않았다는 점과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-08-006 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
By the third week of drought, Marta had stopped asking permission to climb to the roof. Marta nodded and kept filling her buckets. Later that afternoon, though, she carried two of them up to the widow on the fourth floor before watering a single tomato. Pavel, writing his report on the steps, crossed out a line and wrote another beneath it. Pigeons gathered along the tank's rim, dipping their beaks where a rivet leaked.

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) It recounts how a surveyor from the city measured a rooftop tank during a drought.
B) It explains why the city ministry changed its rules about sharing water in buildings.

D) It suggests that a strict family rule can be quietly adjusted by personal judgment.

[해설]
앞부분에서 Marta는 정원이 먼저라는 가문의 규칙을 고수하며 측량사의 말에도 계속 물을 퍼 담는다. 그러나 뒷부분에서 그녀는 토마토보다 먼저 4층 과부에게 물을 가져다주고, Pavel도 보고서의 문장을 고친다. 두 장면을 이으면 규칙이 공식적으로 폐기되지 않아도 개인의 판단으로 조용히 바뀐다는 점이 드러나므로 정답은 D이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 규정 변경의 이유를 다루지 않으며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-08-007 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]

Twenty years earlier he had promised to come home when their mother fell ill, and he had not. Now, setting the last box down, he said he was sorry. Liesel kept chalking. She did not answer, but when she reached the end of the hall she left a gap in the line, an arm's width, just in front of their mother's door. Outside, the 4:45 groaned up the switchback, its windows yellow, carrying no one who would get off.

[질문] Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) A late apology can unsettle a division even when it is not openly accepted.
B) Two siblings divide the rooms of a house that their mother left to them.
C) Anselm failed to return home when his mother became seriously ill.
D) Families can always repair their quarrels if people simply apologize.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
앞부분에서 Liesel은 복도에 분필로 경계선을 긋고, Anselm의 늦은 사과에도 대답하지 않는다. 그러나 뒷부분에서 그녀는 어머니의 방문 앞에 선을 끊어 틈을 남기며, 말없이 분리가 흔들렸음을 보여 준다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 배경 사실일 뿐 글의 요지가 아니며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-08-008 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Rashid taught oud in the cellar beneath our building in Cairo, and when the pipes burst one February the water rose to his knees in an hour. I helped him carry out the instruments. Rashid never complained about the will; he simply kept tuning the oud each week and setting it beside Tariq's chair. That morning Tariq waded in before any of us and lifted it above the water first, holding it the way Rashid held it. Neither said anything. B) It suggests that a bond between teacher and student can form through shared care.

### lit40-medium-08-009 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]

Father had never written down his recipe for the glue, only shown it, and Anders assumed it had died with him. ### lit40-medium-08-010 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
